key_insight: AEGIS is a domain-focused forensic benchmark showing that detecting and localizing AI-generated academic images is still hard: across 7 academic categories and 39 fine-grained subtypes, even GPT-5.1 only achieves 48.80% overall detection and expert models attain just 30.09% localization IoU.
problem_solved: Fills the gap of lacking domain-specific, fine-grained evaluation for forensic analysis of academic images, exposing real-world difficulties that generic benchmarks miss.
method: Curated a domain-specific dataset spanning 7 academic categories and 39 fine-grained subtypes to capture intrinsic forensic complexity.
Simulated four diverse forgery scenarios to test both detection and localization robustness across realistic manipulation styles.
Benchmarked state-of-the-art detectors and localization models (e.g., GPT-5.1), evaluating both detection accuracy and localization IoU to quantify weaknesses.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a realistic, fine-grained testbed to diagnose failure modes in image-forensics systems and prioritize improvements in detection and localization for academic imagery.
visual_elements: Dataset composition treemap/sunburst showing 7 categories and 39 subtypes (proportion per subtype).
Bar chart comparing overall detection rates across models (highlight GPT-5.1 at 48.80%).
Side-by-side example panels of original, forged, and model localization overlays (showing low IoU cases).
Heatmap or table of localization IoU by category/subtype to highlight hard niches (e.g., IoU = 30.09% for experts).
paper_title: AEGIS: A Holistic Benchmark for Evaluating Forensic Analysis of AI-Generated Academic Images
paper_authors: Bo Zhang, Tzu-Yen Ma, Zichen Tang, Junpeng Ding, Zirui Wang
